newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-DUTCH PTT BID FOR TNT SEEN SUCCESSFUL.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-DUTCH PTT BID FOR TNT SEEN SUCCESSFUL.

text.p: Dutch telecoms and postal group Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) on Wednesday launched a US$1.6 billion takeover bid for world-wide transport group TNT Ltd , aiming to create Europe's largest fast- post business.
A combined KPN-TNT group would be in the world's top four time-sensitive freight and logistics groups and have annual revenues of over A$6 billion (US$4.4 billion).
The Australian-based TNT said in a joint statement with KPN it would recommend shareholders accept KPN's A$2.45 per share cash offer. This was 50 percent above TNT's previous close.
Analysts and brokers said the sheer size of the premium and TNT's recommendation meant the bid was likely to deter any potential rivals like Federal Express Corp and ensure its succesful completion.
"What they've done is said 'We don't want to get into a bidding war -- here's A$2.45 -- end of story'," said ABN AMRO Hoare Govett transport analyst Damien Horth.
"I'd be very surprised if Fedex trys to beat it."
Horth added: "My feeling is TNT is not going to be listed on the Australian Stock Exchange for too much longer."

KPN and TNT said the bid represented a multiple of 19.1 times TNT's earnings before interest, tax and abnormal items in the year to June 30, 1996 and a multiple of 2.6 times net assets per share as at June 30.
Analysts said multiples of 10 to 15 times were more usual in acquisitions like this, although they noted TNT's profits had been low by industry standards in recent years.

KPN and TNT said the takeover agreement followed long discussions between KPN and TNT about combining TNT's GD Express Worldwide time sensitive freight and logistics business with KPN's postal subsidiary, PTT Post.
KPN is 45 percent owned by the Dutch government.
"It will create a new global force in the time sensitive distribution and logistics industry, ranking in the top four world-wide," KPN and TNT said.
TNT shareholders and brokers immediately welcomed the bid, shunting TNT's share price up 50 percent to A$2.44 in frantic early trade.
"That's a sensational deal and shareholders won't be able to get out quick enough," James Capel director of institutional sales Stephen Streeter said.

TNT's share price leapt 81 cents or 50 percent to A$2.44 in immediate response to the agreed bid, before easing back to A$2.42 at the close. KPN later confirmed it had bought 9.9 percent of TNT's shares in the market.
KPN chairman and chief executive Wim Dik said the TNT acquisition would help KPN grow quickly outside its home market.
KPN said it would fund the takeover from working capital and and a 2.25 billion guilders (A$1.7 billion) revolving credit facility arranged and underwritten by Goldman Sachs.

Dik said the acquisition would be slightly earnings positive in the calendar 1997 year and said KPN would consider whether to sell those TNT assets not related to time sensitive freight and logistics within the next year.
Ratings agency Standard & Poors affirmed KPN's AA plus long term credit rating and put TNT's B plus rating on creditwatch positive.
KPN's shareholders also welcomed the deal, pushing its share price up 2.10 guilders to 61.00 guilders in early European trade on Wednesday.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
